Sounds like you have successfully installed Thunderbird, it's setting up your email account that's a problem. Sounds pedantic, but it's in important distinction. Reinstalling the program in a case like this is unlikely to help. We need to know some basic information to try to troubleshoot:

- What version of Thunderbird?

- What is your operating system?

- Who is your email provider?

- Is this an IMAP account or POP3?

- What error messages do you see? Please quote them precisely and in full. Screen shots would suffice.

- Your preferences, saved emails, and account information is all stored in your "Profile". Its location depends on your OS (for example, in Windows, it's usually located at "C:\Users\<your Windows user account>\AppData\Roaming\Thunderbird" . If you have an intact copy of the Profile, it may make recovery much easier. Do you know if your Profile is still accessible?

content:
I believe that error message happens when Thunderbird queries the server for setup parameters but is unable to get a result. It could be that Sonic is having server problems, or its settings database is unreachable. You could try again tomorrow, or try setting it up manually rather than letting Thunderbird guess the server settings.

From what I find on Sonic's help page ( https://help.sonic.com/hc/en-us/articles/235251487-General-IMAP-POP3-Settings ), the settings should be:

Incoming Server Type: IMAP Incoming Server Name: imap.sonic.net Port: 993 User Name: <usually your email address> Connection Security: SSL/TLS Authentication method: Normal password

SMTP Server Name: mail.sonic.net SMTP Port: 465 Connection Security: SSL/TLS Authentication method: Normal password User Name: <usually your email address>

When you start to Add a New email account, once you fill in your name and address, a link appears that says "Configure Manually". When you click that, you will have a chance to enter all the configuration manually. Then click the "Re-test" button, and hopefully you'll get the green "The following settings were found by probing the given server" banner. If so, click the Done button and things should be working.

Another possibility is that your Anti=-Virus is blocking communication with the server. But try the above, and if that doesn't work, we can work on the second possibility.


Please let us know how it goes.

content:
The general answer is, Yes, install over the current version. But prepare in advance by checking a couple of things...

- What is your operating system?

- Is your current Thunderbird 46-bit or 32-bit?

- Determine where your current version is from. That is, was in installed from an installer downloaded from the official source ( https://www.thunderbird.net/en-US/thunderbird/all/ )? Or was it installed from a "store", like Microsoft or Apple?


If it was installed from thunderbird.net, download the latest release version from the link above, making sure you get the installer with the same "bitness" as your current. You can install right over the old version and your data should remain intact.

Note that I said SHOULD. Just to be safe, as with all things computer, it's good practice to make a safety copy of your Profile, just in case something goes wrong. This article explains how:

https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profiles-where-thunderbird-stores-user-data#w_backing-up-a-profile

It's also good practice to make regular backups of your Profile if your email store is precious to you.

Otherwise, most email providers delete Trash messages after some period of time.
